title: Weighted SLO Drift Detector and Cost-Normalized Auto-Rollback Gate
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem statement: Current auto-rollback rules are single-metric and static (e.g., P95 latency > Xms). This leads to noisy rollbacks for transient spikes and missed regressions when cost or throughput regressions occur without obvious latency/error spikes. We need a unified, tunable detector that fuses latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput signals into a single weighted departure score and exposes a cost-normalized auto-rollback gate that adapts thresholds per-cohort.
proposal_summary: Introduce a Weighted SLO Drift Detector (WSDD) that computes a normalized departure score across multiple SLO signals, applies cohort-aware thresholds and hysteresis, and drives an Auto-Rollback Gate. The gate has two modes: alert-only (notify on threshold breach) and auto-rollback (initiate traffic evacuation and rollout revert when emergency thresholds are exceeded). Threshold tuning is data-driven using historical incidents and shadow traffic experiments to derive sensible defaults and per-customer sensitivity multipliers.
design_highlights: 1) Signals: P95 latency, P99 latency, 5XX error rate (per-route), tokens-per-request cost (normalized to $/token), and 1m throughput (rps). 2) Normalization: for each signal s compute z = (current - baseline_mean)/baseline_std where baseline is last 7d rolling window with exclusion of known incidents. 3) Weighting: apply configurable weights w_s per-signal; default weights favor latency and error rate but include cost and throughput as first-class signals (example default weights: latency P95=0.35, error rate=0.30, cost/token=0.15, throughput delta=0.20). 4) Departure score = sum(w_s * max(0, z_s)). 5) Thresholds: two thresholds per cohort: warn_threshold (e.g., 2.5) and emergency_threshold (e.g., 5.0). 6) Hysteresis: require sustained breach window (default 3m for warn, 30s for emergency) and minimum sample count. 7) Cohort-aware: thresholds scaled by cohort volatility multiplier computed from baseline stddev; high-noise cohorts get larger thresholds. 8) Cost-normalized emergency: if cost signal dominates (e.g., >60% contribution) we apply a higher sensitivity for paid customers with cost controls enabled.
algorithm_and_ops: - Baseline computation: sliding 7d window rolling mean & std dev, excluding blackout windows. - Real-time scoring: compute z-scores per incoming 10s window, aggregate to 1m resolution. - Auto-rollback decision: if departure_score >= emergency_threshold AND sustained for emergency_window then: 1) open deployment gate (move canary back to baseline or redirect to fallback model), 2) create incident with prefilled playbook, 3) annotate the rollout and create a rollback PR link. - Alerting: two parallel channels (PagerDuty for emergency auto-rollbacks, Slack #rollouts-warnings for warn-level). - Safety nets: allowlist for customers and routes excluded from auto-rollback; manual pause switch in Console; exponential backoff on churn prevention (prevent repeated flip-flops).
tuning_plan: 1) Offline sweep: on historical rollouts and incidents (last 12 months) run a grid search over weights and k-multipliers (threshold = baseline_mean + k * baseline_std) to maximize F1 for detecting actionable regressions while minimizing false positives. Record suggested defaults. 2) Shadow traffic tests: deploy WSDD in alert-only mode to 10 production rollouts with 100% shadow traffic for 2 weeks and capture precision/recall. 3) Canary A/B: run A/B where 10% of canaries are auto-rollback-enabled with conservative params and 90% are alert-only; compare rollback rate, customer impact, time-to-detection. 4) Finalize defaults after one iteration and publish to Console recommendations for customers to tune weights and sensitivity.
acceptance_criteria: - WSDD computes departure score in prod telemetry pipeline at 1m resolution for all canary rollouts. - Default thresholds reduce false positive rollbacks by >= 40% compared to current single-metric P95 rule on historical data set. - Shadow/Canary experiments show precision >= 0.75 for emergency_threshold when run in alert-only mode. - Auto-rollback path executed in a controlled dry-run (no traffic change) and generated expected incident, PR, and console annotation. - Console exposes per-cohort threshold override and an on/off toggle for auto-rollback per-project.
implementation_tasks: - INSTR-1: Add z-score computation module to metrics pipeline and a departure scorer (ENG PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/782). - INSTR-2: Add cohort volatility estimator and persistence (low-latency cache). - INSTR-3: Implement Auto-Rollback Gate controller in rollout-service; integrate with routing layer to move traffic (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-service/pull/254). - INSTR-4: Console UI: threshold controls, on/off toggle, and incident links. - INSTR-5: Playbooks & runbooks update (Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/WSDD+Design).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive auto-rollbacks for noisy routes. Mitigation: cohort volatility scaling and default to alert-only for cohorts with high variance. Risk: mis-calibrated cost signal causing rollbacks on high-value low-latency drops. Mitigation: cost contribution cap (max 40% effective weight) and require at least one reliability metric (latency or error) to be elevated for auto-rollback. Risk: operational complexity for customers. Mitigation: sensible defaults, clear Console UX, and opt-in for auto-rollback with explicit consent for enterprise customers.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for z-score math and scoring logic. - Integration test: synthetic traffic generator that simulates latency, error, and token cost regressions to validate departure score mapping and hysteresis behavior. - Load test: verify scoring at 1m resolution across 10k TPS routing fanout. - Shadow run: 14-day run in alert-only mode with GitHub issue + dashboard capturing metrics. Dashboard: Grafana board 'WSDD / Rollouts' (https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/WSDD-rollouts).
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Deploy scorer to telemetry sandbox and run unit/integration tests (1 week). Phase 1: Alert-only shadow traffic to selected rollouts (2 weeks). Phase 2: Canary auto-rollback for low-risk cohorts with emergency_threshold high (2 weeks). Phase 3: Broader enablement with defaults and Console toggle (2--4 weeks). Manual rollback kill-switch available throughout.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics to surface: departure_score, per-signal z-scores, cohort volatility, rollback_count, false_positive_rate (tracked vs. incident classification), time_to_revert. Alerts: P0 pager on emergency auto-rollback; P1 Slack digest for warn breaches. Dashboards linked in testing_plan.
operational_playbook: - When an auto-rollback fires: 1) Pager notifies on-call; 2) Rollout-service triggers traffic evacuation; 3) automated incident includes: route, model version, departure score snapshot, contributing signals with percentages, suggested rollback PR link; 4) post-mortem must classify whether auto-rollback was correct and update weights if needed.
